summary: Upgraded the ClientApp from Angular 19.2 to Angular 20.3 with `ng update @angular/core@20 @angular/cli@20`. Angular's own migrations did all the work: `moduleResolution` moved to "bundler", the generation defaults were pinned in angular.json to keep the pre-v20 naming style, and the one deprecated `TestBed.get` call became `TestBed.inject`. The hop file listed no related packages, but @ngrx/* 19 pins `@angular/core@^19.0.0`, so @ngrx was bumped to 20.1.0; no hand-written code fixes were needed. `npm install`, `npm run build` and `npm run build:ssr` pass; `npm run test` still fails for the same pre-existing reason as at baseline.
changes: Angular packages 19.2.25 -> 20.3.34; @angular/cli and @angular-devkit/build-angular ^19.2.27 -> ^20.3.41, @angular/compiler-cli and @angular/language-service ^19.2.25 -> ^20.3.34. typescript (~5.8.3) and zone.js (~0.15.1) were already inside the Angular 20 peer ranges, so the CLI left them alone.

tsconfig.json: the CLI migration changed `moduleResolution` from "node" to "bundler", the default for Angular 20 workspaces. Nothing in src/ relies on Node-style resolution (no extension-less deep imports into CJS-only packages), and both the browser and server builds compile unchanged.

angular.json: the CLI migration added a `schematics` block (`type: component/directive/service` and `typeSeparator: "."` for guard/interceptor/module/pipe/resolver). Angular 20 changed the default file/class naming for newly generated code; this block pins the old style guide behaviour, so it only affects future `ng generate` runs and no existing file was renamed.

src/app/services/employee.service.spec.ts: the core migration replaced `TestBed.get(EmployeeService)` with `TestBed.inject(EmployeeService)`. `TestBed.get` was removed in v20. Same semantics, and the spec is unaffected by the pre-existing Karma failure's cause.

@ngrx/{store,effects,entity,router-store,store-devtools} ^19.2.1 -> ^20.1.0 via `ng update @ngrx/store@20`. Not listed in the hop file, but required: NgRx 19 declares a peer of @angular/core ^19.0.0. As in the previous hop, the NgRx schematic runner crashed right after writing package.json (`Cannot find module '@angular-devkit/core'` raised from its own 6_0_0 migration during the mid-run node_modules clean), so its migrations did not execute; the app uses no API that NgRx 20 changed (plain `StoreModule.forRoot`/`EffectsModule.forRoot` registration and `createReducer`/`createAction`), and the build confirms it.

Declined all three optional migrations, per the smallest-correct-change rule: `use-application-builder` (keeps the existing `browser`/`server` builders and the aspnet-prerendering SSR setup), `control-flow-migration` (template rewrite, not an upgrade requirement) and `router-current-navigation` (no `Router.getCurrentNavigation` usage in src/).
package-lock.json regenerated by npm; verified with a from-scratch `rm -rf node_modules && npm install` (no --legacy-peer-deps or --force needed), followed by a clean build.
manual_followups: Tests still fail exactly as at baseline and for the same reason: the `test` target in angular.json lists the stylesheet as "styles.css" instead of "src/styles.css", so Karma reports "Can't resolve 'styles.css'" and aborts before running any spec. Fixing that one path would let the suite run; left alone here because the hop rules only require that a baseline failure not get worse.
rxjs is still ^6.6.7. Angular 20 and NgRx 20 both still accept it, but rxjs 6 is end-of-life and Angular 21 is expected to require rxjs 7; plan the rxjs 7 bump as part of the next hop.

The app remains NgModule-based (every component explicitly `standalone: false`) on the deprecated `browser`/`server` builders with aspnet-prerendering SSR. The `use-application-builder` migration is still pending and is likely to become mandatory in Angular 21, where the old builders are slated for removal.

Deprecated/legacy devDeps remain unchanged (tslint, codelyzer, protractor, node-sass, core-js 2, @types/node 12, jasmine 3.10, karma). None are exercised by the required checks, but karma is deprecated in favour of the Vitest/Web Test Runner builders and codelyzer/tslint block a move to ESLint.
